title: Review: jmap-client iteration 3
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — Two issues (JMAP-bu1.1 and JMAP-bu1.3) represent an API design decision that cannot be undone without a breaking change once callers exist. The window to fix is now, before public release. The other risks are documentation/spec-precision issues with plausible but low-frequency real-world impact.
Confidence: 10% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: JMAP-bu1.4 (SSE .trim() vs RFC 8895 one-space strip — low real-world impact since event IDs with meaningful surrounding whitespace are pathological). Uncertainty driven by: no live server testing; SSE and WebSocket code paths are only unit-tested with mocks, not against a real JMAP server sending edge-case frames. Would raise confidence if: integration test against an actual JMAP server (Cyrus, JMAP Proxy) exercising reconnect with Last-Event-ID.
